answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: each agent locks a modest stake in an escrow contract, a dune of collateral that makes mass-minting fake identities costly while staying affordable for one honest participant. Reputation is then earned only through peer-attested work, the way a comet earns its tail by completing a real orbit instead of flashing briefly, so stake-skipping sybils stay at zero trust. A verified work history layered like the fire inside an opal can later substitute for part of the bond, letting long-lived honest agents reduce their locked capital.
